We have a target molecule: C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2. This is a stilbene derivative with two anisole (methoxy phenyl) groups attached to a central C=C double bond, i.e., 4-methoxy-stilbene? Actually structure: central C=C with each side attached to phenyl with OMe at para? The SMILES: C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2. That's trans? Anyway.

We need retrosynthesis route with at most 1 step (i.e., direct from commercially available precursors). Leaves must be commercially available chemicals, total price <= $150. We don't have price data, but we can assume typical reagents like 4-bromoanisole and 4-methoxyacetophenone? The template we found (ID 223474) gives precursors: COc1ccc(Br)cc1 (4-bromoanisole) and COc1ccc(C(C)=O)cc1 (4-methoxyacetophenone). Reaction appears to be a Heck coupling? Actually product is stilbene with one side methoxy phenyl and other side methoxy phenyl? Wait product from those precursors: 4-bromoanisole + 4-methoxyacetophenone -> product is C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2. That matches: coupling of aryl bromide with aryl ketone? The template seems to convert a carbonyl (acetophenone) to alkene via elimination? Might be a Wittig? But the template gave product.
